use: Style evidence only; never copy phrases, facts, numbers or identity.
method: Roster weights normalized over available eligible donors; equal mass per donor post; sentence mass equal within post. UTC cadence over observed scrape interval. Signature lift is weighted cluster document frequency divided by unweighted eligible all-donor document frequency (3-word EN / 4-character ZH n-grams, present in at least 2 cluster posts).

qualitative.voice_summary: A fast, practitioner voice from people who trade and price options, mostly on short-term index volatility, dealer positioning and chart levels. Posts move between dense, number-heavy positioning reads, terse reactions to charts or links, risk-discipline lessons and frequent promotion of webinars, media appearances or products. The register runs from technical and precise to irreverent desk banter, with judgments usually tied to a stated level, condition or personal position.

qualitative.variation_notes: Length swings widely, from emoji or single-line reactions to multi-paragraph mechanism explanations and long positioning reads. The register moves between precise options terminology, coaching tones and crude banter, depending on the donor and the moment. Hooks are mostly direct claims, with occasional questions, ticker leads, quoted lines and event notices. Promotional and community posts are common alongside the analytical ones, so not every post carries a market view.
qualitative.judgment_style: Mostly assertive and specific, but the strongest market calls are often framed as conditionals tied to a level or signal (what confirms, what fades) rather than unconditional predictions. Data such as levels, implied versus realized moves and returns serves as the support for a view, not as an end in itself. Personal positioning and stops are used to show conviction and risk limits. Explicit hedging words are uncommon, and uncertainty is shown through 'we shall see' style deferral or through scenario framing.
